History:
- Presenting complaint: Persistent dry cough and rhinorrhea for ~5–6 days; cough is continuous, worse at night, and disturbs sleep.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms began ~5–6 days ago; initial brief diarrhea at onset resolved; cough has persisted and not improved.
- Associated symptoms: Subjective chills/feeling feverish (no temperature measured), generalized myalgias and marked fatigue/weakness, throat irritation from coughing; no nausea/vomiting, no current diarrhea.
- Respiratory status: No baseline dyspnea reported; transient breathlessness during coughing fits; no chest pain.
- Context/other: Lives with partner (partner currently well). Former smoker (quit ~6 months). Drinks wine (2–3 glasses on ~3 evenings/week); advised to cut down.

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Hypertension.
- Medications: Metformin — dose/route/frequency not documented; Lisinopril — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: None reported.
- Prior hospitalizations: Not recorded.

Physical Examination:
- Vital signs: Not recorded.
- General: Patient reports marked fatigue and myalgias.
- ENT: Throat irritated from coughing; no increased pain with swallowing reported. Ears reported normal, no pain or discharge.
- Lungs/chest: Dry, continuous cough audible during visit; clinician noted no mucoid sputum production. No baseline increased breathlessness; no chest pain.
- Neuromuscular: Generalized muscle aches limiting activity.
- Other exam elements: Not recorded.
- Orientation/mental status: Not recorded.

Impression:
- Most likely diagnosis: Viral upper respiratory infection/acute bronchitis — presentation consistent with 5–6 day history of rhinorrhea, continuous dry nocturnal cough, myalgias and subjective fever.
- Additional plausible diagnoses consistent with the transcript (from DDx):
  - Influenza — compatible given chills, prominent myalgias and functional impairment.
  - COVID-19 — possible given dry cough, myalgias and transient diarrhea (no testing performed).
  - ACE inhibitor–related cough (lisinopril) — possible alternative contributor but less likely given coincident systemic viral symptoms.

Management Plan:
- Symptomatic care advised:
  - Rest and increased oral fluids.
  - Regular paracetamol recommended for symptomatic relief (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Temporary time off work recommended (1–2 days) to rest; consider returning early next week if improving.
- Safety-netting / follow-up:
  - Return or re-assess if symptoms are not improving in 2–3 days.
  - Seek earlier review if breathing worsens, new chest pain, high/ongoing fever, or other clinical deterioration.
  - If cough and fever persist despite conservative management, clinician may consider antibiotics for possible secondary chest infection.
- Lifestyle advice:
  - Advised to reduce alcohol intake (practical strategy suggested: cut down to 2 glasses/week then reassess).

Patient Summary:
- April presents with a 5–6 day history of a continuous dry cough and runny nose with subjective fever/chills, myalgias and fatigue; initial brief diarrhea resolved. Most likely a viral upper respiratory infection/acute bronchitis. She was advised symptomatic treatment (rest, fluids, paracetamol), short work absence, and to return for review if not improving in 2–3 days or sooner for worsening breathing.

Key Takeaways:
- Rest, stay well-hydrated, and use regular paracetamol for symptom relief.
- Take 1–2 days off work if possible; return when feeling better.
- Come back sooner if breathing becomes worse or if no improvement in 2–3 days (antibiotics may be considered if persistent fever/cough).

Next Steps:
- No investigations or prescriptions ordered at this visit.
- Planned follow-up: re-evaluate in 2–3 days if persistent symptoms; earlier review for deterioration.
- Consider diagnostic testing (e.g., influenza/COVID-19) or antibiotics if clinical course worsens or fails to improve — to be decided on re-assessment.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs (temperature, pulse, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, blood pressure), focused physical exam findings, medication doses/routes/frequencies, smoking pack-years, immunization status (influenza/COVID), and any recent COVID/influenza testing — none recorded in transcript.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted — DDx aligns with transcript conclusions. (If any disagreement had existed it would be flagged as “conflict noted.”)
- Transcript quality comment: Audio transcript generally clear with occasional brief overlaps; clinical history adequate for a provisional assessment but lacks objective vitals and formal exam documentation.
